text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel promises to reduce tax by 20 to 30 billion marks. Reform proposed in several stages starting 1999. Maximum income tax rate will be 40 percent
- IG Metall metal workers trade union ready for pay talks. Klaus Zwickel says he is prepared to call a strike over sick pay cuts
- Liberal Free Democrats (FDP) say the monopoly in the postal sector must end in 1998 at the latest
- Proests against pay cuts spread. A day of action against Daimler-Benz is called.
- Eastern Europe is becoming increasingly important for the German economy. Trade volumes are expected to double by the year 2000.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel wants top income rate of 40 percent and minimum taxation of 20 percent. His tax cutting concept envisages a reduction of 20 to 30 billion marks taxes
- Only criminals could face deportation. Bosnian refugees must leave Bavaria today
- Specially reduced telephone rates for German Unity Day
- Cuts in holiday and Christmas bonuses.
- German investment goes increasingly to eastern Europe
HANDELSBLATT

- Finance Minister Theo Waigel favours cutting taxes by 20 to 30 billion marks. The Christian Democrats and its Bavarian sister party the Christian Social Union want to reduce minimum income tax rate from 25.9 percent to 20 percent and the maximum from 53 percent to 40 percent
- OeTV public sector workers' union say despite being low on funds they could still go on strike
- Eastern Europe takes Asia over in terms of trade volumes. German trade with Eastern Europe is expected to double by the end of the century
- More protests at Daimler-Benz and Opel also plans to cut sick pay. Klaus Zwickel leaders of IG Metall, the metal workers' union, says he is prepared to come to the negotiating table for pay talks
DIE WELT
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel wants to cut taxes
- Trade with eastern Europe grows rapidly
- Klaus Zwickel, leader of IG Metall metalworkers union, wants early pay talks
- OeTV public sector workers union has trouble closing ranks. The east Germans delegates in the union feel their interests are being neglected
